title: Planning Gove’s next chapter together
body_markdown:
## Putting the community at the centre


This is a critical period of planning and action for Gove and we're working together towards a smooth transition for the town of Nhulunbuy that benefits the peninsula.


It’s a simple principle for me: if a community has supported an operation for decades, that community should be supported through the transition that follows.


Together with the Gove Peninsula Futures Reference Group, governments and Traditional Owners, we’re mapping future land use options, understanding how we can support employees who want to stay in the region, and strengthening the community’s skills and business prospects beyond mining.


Our role is to support our partners and their vision for the future of the region, which includes responding to some of the immediate challenges facing the community today.


One of the biggest challenges in Nhulunbuy is housing availability, particularly for essential workers who need to relocate to and stay in the region. We have offered to release 25 of our houses, which had been occupied by our employees, by the end of this year to help address that need. Since 2025, we’ve offered a 22% concession on electricity and water charges, reducing costs for eligible local organisations that support community programs across Nhulunbuy and Yirrkala. And we’re investing more than $11 million in infrastructure projects over 2026-7, including resealing the airport road and intersection upgrades, in addition to our regular maintenance and operating activities.


## Building skills and opportunities for the future


Preparing for transition also means strengthening local skills and future readiness well before mining ends.


We’ve partnered with Charles Darwin University on a future skills study to map training pathways for Yolŋu organisations, and made a significant contribution to the Barawun Centre in Yirrkala to improve its infrastructure and help people find jobs.


We’re funding[a multi-year careers program across 6 local schools](https://www.riotinto.com/en/news/stories/building-future-pathways-gove) to help young people prepare for opportunities in a post-mining economy, and working with Marngarr Resource Centre on a financial literacy and empowerment pilot for households.


Our commercial partnerships with local businesses are another important part of this work. For example, while we have been customers of Gulkula mine for many years, we are looking forward to partnering with them to mine some of our bauxite reserves in our final years of operation. We also continue our important partnership with Rirratjingu Fuel and Cambridge Gulf to supply fuel for our operations through to the end of mining.


These relationships support our operations today while helping strengthen local capability and opportunity for the future.
